``` ::: ::: # Slot 1 — ARX–API ridge regression {#sec-model1} ## Overview A **persistence-free linear model**: the predictors are non-linear functions of the *forcing only* ($P$, $PET$, day of year); no observed or simulated $Q$ enters the right-hand side, so the comparison with the conceptual slots is fair (a catchment model also only sees $P$ and $PET$). The two ideas that lift it above a naive regression are (i) **antecedent precipitation indices** (API), the oldest storage proxy in hydrology and the backbone of IHACRES-type models [@jakeman1993], and (ii) a **Box–Cox target transform** [@box1964] with a bias-corrected back-transform [@duan1983], which handles the extreme skew of daily $Q$ (a02: skew 6.85). Estimation is ridge regression [@hoerl1970], i.e. closed form, so one model evaluation costs one $\sim 22 \times 22$ linear solve. **Why for the Leaf River.** a02 shows that the $R^2$ of a linear model on lagged $P$ rises monotonically with the lag window (0.59 at 10 d → 0.65 at 365 d): most of the daily signal *is* input memory. This slot quantifies exactly how much, and thereby prices the conceptual structure of slots 2–4. ## Conceptual diagram ```{mermaid} flowchart LR P[P_t] --> L["lagged rain

× bias factor c"] B --> Q[["Q̂_t (mm/d)"]] ``` ## Perceptual → conceptual assumptions *Represented*: catchment wetness memory at three time scales; a variable runoff coefficient through the $P_t \times A_t$ interaction terms; the drying effect of accumulated PET; residual seasonality. *Ignored*: mass conservation (nothing forces $\sum \hat Q \le \sum P$ except the bias factor), explicit states, threshold behaviour beyond the quadratic/interaction terms, and any non-stationarity. ## Mathematical formulation Recursive feature states, computed forward over the contiguous forcing frame with zero initial values: $$A^{(j)}_t = \lambda_j\,A^{(j)}_{t-1} + P_t,\qquad j \in \{\text{fast},\text{med},\text{slow}\},\qquad A^{(j)}_{-1}=0 $$ {#eq-api} $$E^{\text{ant}}_t = \lambda_e\,E^{\text{ant}}_{t-1} + \mathrm{PET}_t,\qquad E^{\text{ant}}_{-1}=0 $$ {#eq-eant} The effective memory of @eq-api is $1/(1-\lambda_j)$ days, hence the bounds in @tbl-p1 (1.4–5 d, 5–20 d, 20–1000 d), which bracket the a02 response lag (1–3 d), recession time (9.1 d) and the GAGES-II contact time (549 d). Design row (with $n_\ell = $ `n_lag`, $d_t$ = day of year, $\omega = 2\pi/365.25$): $$ \mathbf{z}_t = \Big[\,1,\; P_t,\dots,P_{t-n_\ell},\; A^{(f)}_t, A^{(m)}_t, A^{(s)}_t,\; E^{\text{ant}}_t,\; \sqrt{P_t},\; \tfrac{P_t A^{(m)}_t}{100},\; \tfrac{P_t A^{(s)}_t}{100},\; \big(\tfrac{A^{(s)}_t}{100}\big)^2,\; \sin\omega d_t,\cos\omega d_t,\sin 2\omega d_t,\cos 2\omega d_t \,\Big] $$ {#eq-design} With $n_\ell = 5$ that is 21 columns including the intercept. Target transform (Box–Cox): $$ y_t = g(Q_t;\lambda_{bc}) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{Q_t^{\lambda_{bc}} - 1}{\lambda_{bc}}, & \lambda_{bc} > 10^{-6}\\[4pt] \ln Q_t, & \text{otherwise,}\end{cases} \qquad g^{-1}(y) = \begin{cases}\big(\max(\lambda_{bc} y + 1,\,10^{-9})\big)^{1/\lambda_{bc}}\\ e^{y}\end{cases} $$ {#eq-boxcox} ($Q>0$ always, a02, so no offset is needed.) Order of operations within day $t$ (explicit Euler / operator splitting): **(1) Recharge (soil routine).** $$R_t = P_t\left(\frac{SM_{t-1}}{FC}\right)^{\beta},\qquad SM^{*} = SM_{t-1} + P_t - R_t$$ {#eq-hbv1} If $SM^{*} > FC$, move the excess to recharge: $R_t \leftarrow R_t + (SM^{*}-FC)$, $SM^{*} \leftarrow FC$. **(2) Actual evaporation.** $$E_{a,t} = \mathrm{PET}_t \cdot \min\!\left(\frac{SM^{*}}{LP\cdot FC},\,1\right),\qquad SM_t = \max\!\big(SM^{*} - E_{a,t},\,0\big)$$ {#eq-hbv2} (if the $\max$ clips, reduce $E_{a,t}$ by the clipped amount so mass is conserved). **(3) Percolation.** $$\mathrm{PERC}_t = \min\big(\mathrm{PERC},\; S_{UZ,t-1} + R_t\big),\qquad S^{*}_{UZ} = S_{UZ,t-1} + R_t - \mathrm{PERC}_t,\qquad S^{*}_{LZ} = S_{LZ,t-1} + \mathrm{PERC}_t$$ {#eq-hbv3} **(4) Response routine** (with the effective constants $K_0^{\text{eff}}=\max(K_0,K_1)$ and $K_2^{\text{eff}}=\min(K_2,\,0.9K_1)$, see @sec-m3-order): $$Q_{0,t}=K_0^{\text{eff}}\max\!\big(S^{*}_{UZ}-UZL,\,0\big),\qquad Q_{1,t}=K_1 S^{*}_{UZ},\qquad Q_{2,t}=K_2^{\text{eff}} S^{*}_{LZ}$$ {#eq-hbv4} $$S_{UZ,t} = S^{*}_{UZ}-Q_{0,t}-Q_{1,t},\qquad S_{LZ,t}=S^{*}_{LZ}-Q_{2,t}$$ {#eq-hbv5} If $Q_{0,t}+Q_{1,t} > S^{*}_{UZ}$ (possible only for extreme $K$ combinations), scale both down by $S^{*}_{UZ}/(Q_{0,t}+Q_{1,t})$ and set $S_{UZ,t}=0$. **(5) Routing.** Generated runoff $Q^{\text{gen}}_t = Q_{0,t}+Q_{1,t}+Q_{2,t}$ is convolved with the triangular weights obtained by integrating the unit-area isosceles triangle $h(u)$ on $[0,\mathrm{MAXBAS}]$: $$w_j=\int_{j-1}^{j} h(u)\,\mathrm{d}u,\quad j=1..\lceil \mathrm{MAXBAS}\rceil,\qquad h(u)=\frac{4}{\mathrm{MAXBAS}^2}\min\!\big(u,\ \mathrm{MAXBAS}-u\big)_+ $$ {#eq-hbv6} $$w_j \leftarrow w_j\Big/\sum_k w_k,\qquad \boxed{\,Q_t=\sum_j w_j\,Q^{\text{gen}}_{t-j+1}\,}$$ {#eq-hbv7} ## Parameter ordering rule {#sec-m3-order} HBV requires $K_0 \ge K_1 > K_2$. Four things were verified in `src/models/model_1.py`: 1. **Observed discharge never enters the design matrix.** The regressors are precipitation, PET and exponentially-weighted antecedent-precipitation indices. The "AR" in ARX is autoregression in the API *state*, not on observed $Q$ — so the model remains comparable with the conceptual slots, which is exactly what `config/project.yaml -> ml_state_note` requires. 2. **The multiplicative bias factor $c$ is frozen at fit time.** It is computed once inside `fit()` from the fitting window and only *read* in `simulate()`. It is not recomputed from the window being predicted — which would have been a textbook leak, and would have manufactured $\beta \approx 1$ on any period. 3. **Column means and standard deviations are likewise frozen** in `_fitted` and restored by `load()`. 4. **The lazy-fit fallback routes to the calibration window** through the guarded loader, never to the window passed to `simulate()`.
